A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GeoSURGE, with matching architecture, benchmark datasets and main results. All supplied text, equations, figures and tables are readable. v2 includes a two-page supplement; the supplied v1 ends with references and contains no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original GeoSURGE benchmark results, IM2GPS ablations, qualitative examples and evaluations of three standalone vision-language models.

after.justification: v2 retains original GeoSURGE results and reports expanded ablations, additional controls and author-generated baseline results, including in its supplement.

M1.justification: The architecture, semantic fusion and InfoNCE objective remain unchanged. However, v1 Section III.D describes multiplying cosine similarities, while v2 Section 3.4 explicitly applies softmax before multiplying probabilities. The PDFs do not establish whether this changes inference or documents a previously omitted step.

E1.justification: Both versions train on MP-16 and evaluate single-image global geolocation on IM2GPS, IM2GPS3k, YFCC4k, YFCC26k and GWS15k. Extending ablations across these existing benchmarks adds analysis without introducing new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–5 replace Qwen2-72B, InternVL2-76B and NVLM-D-72B comparisons with GeoReasoner results across all five benchmarks and GAEA results on three. Previously missing GeoCLIP and RFM10MS2 comparisons are populated. PIGEOTTO results are also added for GWS15k, explicitly qualified because its sampling differs.

E3.justification: The main training split, optimization settings and Ten Crop evaluation remain unchanged. New controls evaluate finest-partition-only representations and fully frozen CLIP. v2 also corrects the stated distance thresholds from 1/5/25/750/2500 km to 1/25/200/750/2500 km, matching the tables in both versions; this does not establish a changed benchmark computation.

E4.justification: v1's hierarchy, semantic-fusion and geographic-embedding ablations cover only IM2GPS. v2 extends them across all five benchmarks and adds flat-representation comparisons to separate hierarchy from embedding effects, plus frozen-CLIP controls testing the contribution of fine-tuning. These appear in Tables 6–14, including the supplement. The qualitative success and failure examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v2's references to significant improvements do not introduce statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All 25 main GeoSURGE scores remain unchanged, but baseline results are added and removed, and extensive ablation results are introduced. Existing IM2GPS ablation entries also change: five-level street accuracy falls from 24.1 in v1 Table VII to 19.4 in v2 Table 10. Three-block semantic fusion's street gain changes from 3.9 percentage points to an implied 7.2 in Table 11. These are revised reports, not merely relocated tables.

T1.justification: The geographic partition definitions, embedding formulation and InfoNCE equation are retained. Neither version contains additional theorems, proofs or substantive theoretical derivations.

C1.justification: The three headline contributions and the claim of best results on 22 of 25 metrics remain. However, v2's conclusion drops v1's blanket assertion that geographic embeddings improve all distance metrics, retaining the narrower claim that the representations contribute centrally to performance.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that hierarchy and geographic embeddings are complementary and that CLIP fine-tuning improves embedding alignment. The LVLM discussion replaces the argument about retrieval augmentation drawn from standalone-model comparisons with a hypothesis about landmark memorization. Existing explanations of visual ambiguity and sparse geographic training coverage remain.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents softmax normalization, distinguishes the finest partition used in flat controls from the middle partition used in one-level depth ablations, and identifies author-reproduced baseline scores. Core hyperparameters, hardware and training time remain unchanged. The removed standalone LVLM experiments' chain-of-thought and 500-token settings disappear.

R1.justification: v2 adds GeoReasoner and GAEA citations and discussion, while removing references supporting the three deleted standalone LVLM comparisons. It also sharpens the contrast with TransLocator by describing semantic queries as structural guidance. The broader classification, retrieval and hybrid positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, with further revisions to method explanations, results discussion and conclusion. The ablation narrative is reorganized around YFCC26k and GWS15k, while IM2GPS material is integrated into a new supplement alongside other ablations. This exceeds isolated wording or numbering edits.

P2.justification: The document is reformatted and tables substantially reorganized into benchmark-specific panels and supplementary displays. Semantic-fusion tables change from gains alone to absolute accuracies with an explicit no-fusion row. Baseline provenance gains italic and gray formatting. All four figure images are retained, although their placement and sizing change.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical support through ablations across all five benchmarks, new flat-representation and frozen-CLIP controls, and more complete baseline comparisons. Reporting problems temper these gains: revised IM2GPS ablation values are unexplained, and Table 12 reports YFCC4k full-model city/region accuracies of 33.7/49.4, conflicting with 33.6/48.7 in Table 3 and other ablation tables. The expanded evidence improves the paper, but these inconsistencies limit the overall gain.
